data.title: Google says no evidence of widespread Gmail outage
data.description:
Gmail users flooded outage trackers with complaints on Tuesday, but Google says it isn’t seeing signs of a widespread problem.


The tech giant said on Tuesday, November 17, that it had found no evidence of a broad disruption to its popular email service, even as thousands of people reported trouble with their inboxes.


Thousands of users reported problems

By noon ET, outage tracking website Downdetector had logged more than 2,800 reports of issues with Gmail. Most users said they were having trouble receiving emails, while others reported problems getting into the service at all.

The complaints marked a second wave of reports. Downdetector data showed problems had already peaked around 2:40 p.m. ET on Monday before climbing again Tuesday morning.

For many people, Gmail is central to both work and personal life, so even scattered issues can cause headaches, from missed meeting invites to delayed verification codes and receipts.

What Google has said

A Google spokesperson told Rolling Out that the company was not seeing evidence of a broad Gmail service disruption. The spokesperson added that Google’s teams keep a close eye on service health and that real-time updates are always available on the Google Workspace Status Dashboard.

Google shared a similar message in a post on X from its News from Google account, encouraging users to check the dashboard for the latest information. The dashboard tracks the health of Gmail along with other Workspace apps, such as Google Drive and Google Meet.

As of 1:45 p.m. ET, the dashboard did not list any active Gmail disruptions.

The gap between user complaints and Google’s assessment is worth noting. Downdetector tracks reports submitted by users, so a spike signals that many people are noticing problems, but it doesn’t necessarily mean the service is down for everyone. Issues can also stem from individual accounts, devices, internet connections or the providers sending the messages.

A week of tech failures

The Gmail reports follow a rough stretch for some of the country’s biggest systems. In recent days, Americans have dealt with several major disruptions.

  1. A Microsoft Outlook outage last week left users without email for nearly 24 hours.
  2. A telecommunications failure prompted the Federal Aviation Administration to temporarily halt flights nationwide beginning Friday, November. 13.
  3. Chase customers reported login and account problems on Monday.
  4. Marriott’s website and app saw a spike in problem reports Tuesday morning, with hundreds of users reporting trouble with logins and reservations.

Taken together, the incidents have left many people frustrated with the reliability of the digital services they depend on every day. Still, there is no evidence that the Gmail complaints are connected to any of them.

We want to be clear that we aren’t currently seeing evidence of a broad Gmail service disruption, and you can always check real-time status on our Status Dashboard: https://t.co/hXJj1ijxrA

— News from Google (@NewsFromGoogle) November 17, 2026

What to do if Gmail isn’t working

If emails aren’t showing up, there are a few simple steps worth trying.

Start by checking the Google Workspace Status Dashboard to see whether the company has flagged a problem. If nothing is listed, try opening Gmail on a different device or switching between the app and a web browser, since issues sometimes affect one but not the other.

It’s also a good idea to check your spam and other folders, along with any filters you’ve set up, in case messages are being sorted somewhere unexpected. Sending a test email to yourself can show whether messages are coming through. Refreshing the page, updating the Gmail app or restarting your device can also help clear up minor glitches.

Anyone expecting time-sensitive emails may want to give contacts a heads-up or use another way to stay in touch until the issue clears up.

data.title: ARC Raiders patch fixes 50+ bugs, but these 7 remain
data.description:
ARC Raiders Live Update 2.6.0 is now live. Embark Studios brought back the Cold Snap Major Map Condition, added the Outlaw Stencil set for weapon customization and shipped a long list of fixes. The studio also says it is finishing a new project that arrives next week.


What is new in Update 2.6.0?

Cold Snap returns to the Major Map Condition rotation. The Outlaw Stencil set gives players a new way to customize weapons. Embark removed the Beachcombing Minor Map Condition from Riven Tides and expanded the mechanic to all maps.


The Dockmaster’s Detector can now find buried items everywhere except Pendola Pass, where the Mountaineer’s Detector is still required.

Live Update 2.6.0 has landed Topside, bringing a flurry of fixes and improvements to keep your runs smooth – and the Outlaw Stencil set to spruce up your hard-earned weapons.

Read the patch notes here: https://t.co/UeJnKzGjNY https://t.co/n1UsNx7D7h

— ARC Raiders (@ARCRaidersGame) November 17, 2026

What changed on the maps?

Lighting and atmosphere in Spaceport were refined to improve visibility between interiors and exteriors, with less harsh contrast and faster exposure adaptation. Buried City got better visibility in dark interiors, less cloud shadowing and subtle bloom changes.

Collision problems were fixed across Pendola Pass, Spaceport and Riven Tides. Players can now shoot through the railyard windows on Pendola Pass, and a gap behind a cliff where players got stuck was closed. Collision near the Seed Vault Airshaft in Stella Montis was also improved.

Which gameplay bugs were fixed?

Players no longer appear invisible after quickly entering and leaving a Gondola. The Road Warrior skill can recycle Weapon Amplification Modules and Candleberries during raids. Vaulting no longer drains jump stamina, and the Vaults on Vaults on Vaults skill uses none.

Players stay in place during a knockout animation, and a defibrillator revive now prevents an immediate knockout. The Hydra now aims only some weapons at Lure Grenades while still shooting at players. Firework Boxes now delay launches instead of fizzling when many are activated, and Grapple Hook lines cancel correctly if a player is downed.

What weapon changes are included?

The Stiletto’s weight drops from 7 to 6. Aiming down sights with scoped weapons no longer shifts aim sideways. A crosshair issue when moving sideways while aiming at an ARC was fixed. The Snap Hook description now shows its correct 18-meter range.

What interface and progression fixes are included?

Players can now drop items by dragging them outside the inventory. The Outpost can be upgraded to Level 4 after a bug blocked some players. Fixes cover the Ping Wheel getting stuck, Inventory bumper navigation, the Repair button and gamepad looting that could delete items. Quests that could soft lock if an item was lost are fixed. A new Times Revived By A Stranger stat appears in the Codex.

What known issues remain?

Supply drops from the Deep-Space Telescope in Pendola Pass may land out of bounds. The key room in Cielo Sereno Observatory may stay closed after using a key during the ARC Frigate condition.

Vaulting on an ARC Reclaimer can push players off, and players can get stuck in an ARC Turbine as it takes off. A tree near the Water Treatment Control building on Dam Battlegrounds can trap players. Some players cannot finish the When Everything Falls quest.

What is not confirmed?

Embark has not said what the new project arriving next week is. Sources describe a few fixes with slightly different wording, such as the invisibility bugs.

data.title: Alarming cyberattack hits 178 sites, including Zoom and CNN
data.description:
Visitors to some of the internet’s most popular websites may have been exposed to hackers looking to steal their personal and financial information.


Malicious code was planted on websites belonging to 178 organizations, including Zoom, the BBC, CNN, HSBC and IKEA, according to cybersecurity firm Report URI. Its researchers uncovered the attack on Monday, November 16. Other affected names included Salesforce, Equifax, Fox News, Alaska Airlines and GitLab.


The software was built to grab credit card details, reroute cryptocurrency payments and target certain iPhones and iPads. It’s still unclear how many people, if any, had their information stolen.

How the attack happened

Instead of breaking into each organization one by one, the hackers went after a single shared tool. They exploited a weakness in Optimizely, a company whose software lets businesses test different versions of their websites, such as new page layouts or features.

Because so many major companies rely on that service, tampering with it allowed the attackers to slip malicious code onto the websites that used it. That meant people could encounter the harmful software just by loading an affected page.

Optimizely said in a status update on its website on Tuesday that it had fixed the problem and removed the malicious code.

What the code was designed to do

Researchers found the code could carry out several kinds of theft. One method swapped out cryptocurrency wallet addresses that users had copied, which could send payments to the hackers instead of the intended recipients.

The software could also try to steal credit card numbers, pull information saved in web browsers and take screenshots. Some of the code went after iPhones and iPads running older versions of Apple’s operating systems, trying to take advantage of known weaknesses.

In total, Report URI identified 188 affected website scripts across the 178 organizations. Researchers also traced roughly $7,040 in cryptocurrency payments to wallets tied to the attack on Nov. 16, though the full financial damage remains unknown.

The findings don’t necessarily mean hackers broke directly into all 178 companies or stole data from everyone who visited their sites.

Which organizations were affected

The list spans nearly every industry. Banking and finance took the biggest hit, with 32 organizations affected, including several regional HSBC sites, Equifax, Paychex and TaxAct. Technology accounted for 23 names, among them Zoom, Salesforce, GitLab, Bitly and Optimizely itself.

Retailers such as IKEA, ASOS, Mattel, American Eagle and several regional Levi’s sites were also caught up, along with streaming services like Peacock and Starz and news outlets including CNN, the BBC, Fox News and NPR.

Other affected names ranged from KLM and Alaska Airlines to Starbucks Canada, Change.org, UNICEF USA and Mint Mobile. Report URI noted that additional organizations may have been affected beyond those it identified.

How to protect yourself

Anyone who visited an affected website on Nov. 16 should be aware of the potential risks, especially if they entered payment details or sent cryptocurrency. Still, simply opening a website does not mean information was taken.

Here are five steps to take now.

  1. Update your iPhone, iPad and other devices with the latest security updates.
  2. Check your bank accounts for unfamiliar charges, particularly if you entered card details on an affected site.
  3. Review any cryptocurrency transfers to confirm they reached the correct wallet.
  4. Watch for unexpected login alerts or changes to your online accounts.
  5. Contact your bank right away if you spot an unauthorized payment.

Investigators have not yet determined how many people may have been affected.

Source: Newsweek, originally reported by Chris Matthews.

data.title: Microsoft Outlook outage hits UK and US users: Latest updates
data.description:
Microsoft Outlook is down for thousands of users today. The company says it is investigating problems accessing Exchange Online mailboxes and that the issue may affect Microsoft 365 connectivity in any region.


What is happening with Outlook?

Users report that Outlook fails to load, shows a blank inbox or will not send emails. Many see a Failed to fetch error, which appears when a browser sends a request to a server and gets no reply. Reports of problems began in the US around 4 p.m. and in the UK just after 5:20 p.m.


We’re investigating reports of users experiencing issues accessing Exchange Online mailboxes through multiple connection methods in the Americas. More details can be found in the Microsoft 365 admin center under EX1550543.

— Microsoft 365 Status (@MSFT365Status) November 12, 2026

How many people are affected?

Counts differ by source and time. Outage tracker Downdetector showed more than 3,300 UK reports within about 20 minutes, around 60,000 in the US, and other reports cited 39,000 or even nearly 150,000. These numbers change quickly and are user-submitted.

What has Microsoft said?

The company said it is investigating reports of users having trouble accessing Exchange Online mailboxes through multiple connection methods in the Americas. It later said the issue may affect Microsoft 365 connectivity for users in any region. More details are posted in the Microsoft 365 admin center under incident EX1550543. Some users said the admin center was also hard to reach, and the company has not given a fix time.

Are Teams and Copilot affected?

Reports conflict. One outlet says hundreds of UK users had trouble with Teams and Copilot, while another says Teams was not affected, though Copilot showed a spike in reports.

What can you do?

There is no confirmed fix on the user side. Check Microsoft’s 365 status account for updates, try again later and avoid repeatedly resubmitting important emails until service returns.

What is not confirmed?

The cause of the outage and the time of the fix are unknown. One article carries an October date for a similar event, so it may describe an earlier outage. Report counts differ by source.

data.title: Stephanie Humphrey on how to give this season without falling for a holiday scam
data.description:
Stephanie Humphrey spent years as a systems engineer before she turned to helping everyday people use technology with confidence. Known online as TechLifeSteph, she is a consumer technology journalist and broadcast personality whose advice has reached viewers of Good Morning America, GMA3, CNN and Fox 29.


This time of year, her focus is scams. As holiday shopping, travel, deliveries and charitable giving pick up, so do the schemes built to empty bank accounts. The FBI reported $16.6 billion in consumer losses to internet crime in 2024, a 33% jump from the year before.


What got you into tech?

I am a former engineer by education and training. I have two engineering degrees. I worked as an engineer for a number of years, and so this has always been my life. I’m happy now to be able to use different platforms like this, right here on Rolling Out, to help people understand how technology can make their lives easier.

What is the most common holiday scam you’ve seen?

I think for the holidays, we’re going to see a lot of charity scams, because this is the time of year when people tug on those heartstrings. And not just organizational charity scams, but those folks on TikTok with the GoFundMes for their families and things like that.

I’m not saying that we shouldn’t give, because that is what we are called to do, but we have to use a little discernment in researching organizations and really paying attention to where we’re putting our money.

How can you tell when a website is a scam?

You’ve got to pay really close attention to misspellings on the site, typos and things that don’t look right. I know AI is making it really easy to clone websites so they look exactly like the site, but the URL is always going to be a little bit different, because you can’t have the same web address as a legitimate site. So you’ve got to really scrutinize the URL when you’re doing your web surfing.

That’s something a service like Xfinity Shield can help with, because the CyberSecure part of Xfinity Shield does that work for you and alerts you if a website seems malicious. It gets it before you even start clicking and downloading.

How can we keep our elderly parents safe this season?

It’s tough. I go through this with my mom as well. Number one, you have to be patient. They didn’t grow up with this technology. It’s not inherent to how they’re used to operating. I know it’s hard, but you’ve got to be a little bit patient. Walk them through different things.

In addition to protecting your Wi-Fi itself, you can set some family settings in Xfinity Shield that help them. You can block websites, and you can control the content they might have access to right in the app.

But one good tip I tell everybody, especially when it comes to those tech scams where they tell you your grandkid has been kidnapped, have a family code phrase. My family has a code phrase that only we know. Literally, me, my brother and my mom know this phrase. We say it to each other all the time. It’s been an inside joke in our family for a really long time.

Especially with those voice scams, because AI can actually clone my voice and call my mother and say, “Hey, Mom, I’m on the side of the road. My car got in an accident.” Have a family code phrase, not just a code word, because a word is easy to figure out. Then you can ask the person on the other end of the line, “What’s our code phrase?” If they don’t know it, you know it’s a scam.

What should you do in the first hour after you realize you’ve been scammed?

Depending on how much access you’ve given the scammer, number one, shut your bank accounts down, put flags on your credit cards and put holds on all of your financial accounts. Call your bank, call your credit card company and let them know, “I think I’ve been scammed. Freeze everything.” That’s the first thing.

Then you want to go into all of your accounts and change those passwords. If you’re smart with your tech, you should have a password manager that can help make that a little bit easier, so all your passwords are stored, safe and strong.

Again, you’re going to use something like Xfinity CyberSecure to run a diagnostic to make sure that nothing else in your home has been compromised. It’s not just your computer and your smartphone that are connected to your internet. Your TV, your smart speakers, some people’s refrigerators are smart. Any device in your house that has an internet connection is connected to that Wi-Fi, and it needs to be protected as well.

Is Xfinity easy to use for someone who isn’t tech savvy?

So easy to use, because number one, it’s already included. If you’re already an Xfinity customer and you have the advanced Xfinity Gateway, their upgraded router, Xfinity Shield is already in there. There’s not a whole lot you need to do, because as soon as you connect your devices to your Wi-Fi at home, they’re already covered and protected by CyberSecure.

Then you download the app, and now you have CyberSecure and the family settings in there as well. You can control screen time for your kids and block some websites if you need to. You’re going to be able to manage all of that right within the app.

How do people get started?

Just head to xfinity.com and search for Xfinity Shield, and all the info is right there.

Where can people find you?

You can find me all around the web at @techlifesteph, or you can visit my website at stephaniehumphrey.com.

What is one thing people can do right now to be more secure?

You should have two-factor authentication enabled on every single account. That’s where you log in and they text you a code and you’ve got to put the code in. It’s an extra step, I know, but it does still help. It’s not foolproof, but it does still help keep your account secure. So put that two-factor authentication in place.

data.title: Experts Warn Another Internet Outage Could Lock You Out Next
data.description:
A wave of crashes at Microsoft, Apple, JPMorgan Chase and the airlines has specialists urging Americans to protect their money, files and holiday travel before the next failure hits


A run of technology failures this month has left Americans staring at error screens, and cybersecurity experts say the stumbles are less a fluke than a preview.


Since the start of November, a sweeping Microsoft cloud outage has disrupted businesses, health care providers and banks. The Federal Aviation Administration is still investigating a telecommunications breakdown that triggered a nationwide ground stop last Friday. On Monday, thousands of customers reported trouble getting into their online bank accounts, a problem JPMorgan Chase later blamed on a temporary software glitch. United Airlines said a computer issue delayed departing flights that same day, and on Tuesday, Apple said an internal update knocked the App Store and other services offline.

The pileup has fueled online chatter about coordinated attacks and planned blackouts. Experts say the reality is more ordinary, and in some ways more unsettling.

What’s Really Behind the Outage Wave

Michael Chapple, a professor of IT, analytics and operations at the University of Notre Dame, said there is no reason to believe the country is under a cyberattack. He called the timing of the failures largely coincidental but said they expose real weaknesses in the nation’s technology infrastructure, and that more incidents are likely as society leans harder on complicated systems.

Part of the problem is concentration. Feng Li, associate dean for research and innovation at Bayes Business School at City St George’s, University of London, noted that so many services run on the same underlying systems that switching from a bank’s app to its website may not help. A breakdown at one bank, he added, can also delay payments to customers at another.

First, Confirm It’s Not Just You

When an app freezes or a site won’t load, first figure out whether the trouble is widespread. Downdetector compiles user reports of disrupted services, though Kayne McGladrey, a security expert and senior member of the Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, cautioned that its numbers can swell when anxious users pile on during high-profile events.

Sites such as Is It Down Right Now test availability directly, and many companies publish their own real-time status pages. During Tuesday’s disruption, Apple’s System Status page showed whether the App Store was working.

Back Up Your Digital Life

Many Outlook users lost access to their inboxes during the Microsoft failure, a reminder that contacts and documents can become unreachable at the worst moment. Chapple recommends synchronization tools that keep working copies across several devices, such as Google Drive synced to a personal computer, so work can continue even when a provider fails.

Protect Your Money When Banks Go Offline

For working families, a frozen bank app can mean a missed ride, a stalled bill payment or a grocery run cut short. Li suggests carrying a backup card from a different bank. McGladrey goes further, keeping two to four weeks of cash in small bills and spreading his money across institutions and payment types, including a credit card from another issuer, a debit card and, ideally, a credit union account.

Deposits are not the main danger, he said, since FDIC-insured accounts are protected up to $250,000. Scammers are. Fake texts claiming an account has been locked tend to spike during outages, so any unsolicited message about your finances should be treated as hostile. If you need money immediately, visit a branch or an ATM. Otherwise, wait, since these incidents usually clear the same day, and do not resubmit transfers that may already be processing.

Chapple also advises keeping bank security features switched on and using multifactor authentication so unusual activity stands out quickly.

Plan Ahead for Holiday Travel

With technical delays repeatedly hitting airlines this month, experts urge travelers to build in flexibility. Li recommends turning on airline alerts and leaving extra time for fixed-date commitments. McGladrey suggests buffer days around important trips, knowing your rebooking options and insuring expensive nonrefundable tickets. Chapple suggests mapping out alternatives, such as a rental car or a train, since those who react fastest avoid the longest lines.

Even solid preparation will not erase every inconvenience, Chapple acknowledged. Sometimes the only option is turning to other tasks for a few hours.

Li argues the burden should not fall on consumers alone. Regulators, he said, should gather evidence from operators, investigate what went wrong, publish their findings, confirm that backup systems work in practice and tighten rules where needed to prevent a repeat.

Source: HUFFPOST

data.title: Game Awards 2026: Who is nominated and who got left out?
data.description:
The nominees for The Game Awards 2026 are out, and Grand Theft Auto VI leads the way with eight nominations, including Game of the Year, even though it does not release until Thursday, Nov. 19. Host Geoff Keighley revealed the lists in a livestream today. The ceremony takes place Dec. 10 at the Peacock Theater in Los Angeles.


Who are the Game of the Year nominees?

The six nominees are 007 First Light, Control Resonant, Grand Theft Auto VI, Phantom Blade Zero, Resident Evil Requiem and The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time. Last year’s winner was Clair Obscur: Expedition 33.


What did GTA 6 earn?

Besides Game of the Year, it is nominated for Best Game Direction, Best Narrative, Best Art Direction, Best Score and Music, Best Audio Design, Best Action/Adventure and Best Performance for Manni L. Perez. The Performance nod confirms Perez plays Lucia. Variety counts eight nominations, while a Forbes list shows fewer categories, so counts differ by outlet.

Is GTA 6 eligible?

Yes. The eligibility window ends Friday, Nov. 20, and the award releases before that. Some fans suggested the show moved its dates to fit the game. Keighley rejected that and said the calendar is the same every year. Forbes notes the game has no reviews yet, so some voters may have chosen it sight unseen.

Who else is nominated?

Best Ongoing includes Arc Raiders, Final Fantasy XIV, Fortnite, No Man’s Sky and The Witcher 3. Most Anticipated includes Fable, Final Fantasy VII Revelation, God of War Laufey, Resident Evil Veronica and The Witcher 4. Content Creator of the Year includes IShowSpeed, CDawg, Cellbit, LilSimsie and OhnePixel.

Best Multiplayer features Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4, Gears of War: E-Day, Marathon and others.

How are winners picked?

A global jury of more than 100 media outlets and creators chooses nominees, and winners come from a mix of jury and fan votes. Fans can vote at TheGameAwards.com. The show will stream on more platforms than ever, including Disney+, Roblox, YouTube, Twitch, Steam and TikTok Live.

What is not confirmed?

The nomination count for GTA 6 varies by source, and Variety’s story names Grand Theft Auto IV in one line, which looks like a typo. A claim that the cost $2 billion is a rumor. Winners are not decided until Dec. 10.

data.title: GTA 6 vs. your job: Fans are choosing the game
data.description:
Grand Theft Auto VI arrives at midnight Thursday, Nov. 19, and many fans have rearranged work and home life to play from the first minute. It is the franchise’s first new game in more than a decade, and the release has been delayed twice, from 2025 to May 2026 and then to November.


How are fans preparing?

Ciara Singleton, who manages an Airbnb, is weighing a costume party with several TVs and consoles or a theater screening on a friend’s projector. Thomas Gaskins, a father of two teens, took Nov. 19 and 20 off and plans to play until 5 a.m. Dakota Eldridge, an event planner in Kentucky, will take 10 days off while keeping up meal prep and gym sessions.


Software engineer Malcolm Bixby is taking two weeks off and built a spreadsheet for play, sleep and meals. In Texas, Kelsey Rogers got time off after telling her boss the reason, and he said he was also taking days off. She expects her company may not run for two or three days.

Are employers getting involved?

An Army battalion at Fort Stewart, Georgia, is reportedly offering four days off tied to the release in exchange for reenlisting for two to six years. IGN reported that Logitech is giving employees the day off, and its CEO said it is time to retire the idea that gaming is a waste of time.

What is the game about?

Players return to Vice City, a fictional city based on Miami, first seen in 2002. For the first time, players can switch between a male and a female lead, Jason, a former soldier, and Lucia, who has a long rap sheet. Singleton wore a Lucia costume in Miami over Halloween and said strangers recognized her.

What do the numbers show?

One report says the game passed $1 billion in sales a week before release, which would top the domestic box office of the latest Spider-Man film. Analysts estimate the cost above $1 billion, though Take-Two has not given a figure. Take-Two’s CEO called it expensive.

Why does the game resonate?

An Rochester Institute of Technology professor says it offers a funhouse mirror view of America, with references to music, TV and movies that are instantly recognizable.

Are some players trying to play early?

Some Xbox users are changing their console location to a time zone where the game unlocks first, since New Zealand gets it earliest. That workaround is unverified, and the platform terms may not allow it.

What is not confirmed?

The $1 billion cost is an estimate, and the sales milestone comes from one report. The first official sales figures are expected after launch. Whether the Army offer applies across units was not detailed.

data.title: 7 urgent steps to lock down your identity after a breach
data.description:
Seven steps can protect your identity after a data breach notice: verify the notice is real, freeze your credit, change passwords and add two-step verification, get an IRS Identity Protection PIN, monitor your accounts and credit reports, watch for scams and report fraud quickly. A breach does not mean identity theft will happen, but acting fast lowers the risk.


Breaches are common. The FTC received more than 1 million identity theft reports in 2023, and criminals often follow breaches with fake notices and calls. The first two steps matter most, because they confirm the threat and lock the door on new accounts.


1. How do you know the notice is real?

Do not click links or call numbers in the message. Go to the company’s official website or a phone number you already trust and look for the same announcement. Check what was exposed, such as Social Security numbers, financial accounts, health information or passwords, since that decides your next steps.

2. How do you lock your credit?

Freeze your credit with Equifax, Experian and TransUnion. It is free by law, takes minutes and blocks most new accounts opened in your name. It does not hurt your score, and you can lift it temporarily when you apply for credit. A fraud alert is a weaker option. Freeze your children’s credit too if their data was exposed.

3. What should you do about passwords?

Change the password for the breached account and any account where you reused it. Use a password manager, and turn on two-step verification with an authenticator app, which is stronger than text codes.

4. Should you get an IRS PIN?

If your Social Security number was exposed, request an Identity Protection PIN at irs.gov/ippin. It stops anyone else from filing a tax return in your name.

5. How do you monitor your accounts?

Check your credit reports free at AnnualCreditReport.com, set bank and card alerts and review statements and medical insurance explanations of benefits. Sign up for free monitoring if offered, but remember it alerts you after a problem.

6. How do you avoid breach scams?

Criminals impersonate the company, banks and the IRS. Never share codes, passwords or Social Security numbers by phone, text or email unless you started the contact.

7. What if your identity is stolen?

Report it at IdentityTheft.gov, which builds a recovery plan and creates an identity theft report. Contact the fraud departments of affected companies, place an extended fraud alert and dispute errors with the credit bureaus. Keep records of every call and letter.

What should you do today?

Spend 30 minutes on steps 2 and 3: freeze your credit and update passwords. Then set a reminder to review your credit reports every few months.

data.title: 3 reasons GTA 6 preorders are breaking records
data.description:
Grand Theft Auto VI has drawn an estimated $1 billion in digital console preorders ahead of its Nov. 19 launch, according to market research firm Sensor Tower. Neither Rockstar Games nor parent company Take-Two Interactive has confirmed the figures. GTA V needed three days after launch to pass $1 billion in 2013.


How big are the preorder numbers?

Sensor Tower puts digital console preorders at about 10.31 million as of Nov. 11, up from 7.71 million on Nov. 2. PlayStation accounts for roughly 7.73 million copies and $751 million.


Xbox adds about 2.58 million copies and $250 million. That is a 75% to 25% split. The estimated average price of about $97 suggests many buyers chose the $99.99 premium edition over the $79.99 standard version. Sony and Microsoft both say it is the most preordered game in their digital stores. Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick said preorders are running far ahead of expectations.

How does it compare with GTA V?

GTA V earned $815.7 million in its first 24 hours and passed $1 billion within three days. It had about 7 million preorders and sold 11 million copies on day one. This time the milestone arrives before launch. One industry forecast projected $3.3 billion to $5.2 billion in global revenue by the end of the first week.

When can you play, and how big is the download?

Pre-loading began Nov. 10 on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S for anyone who bought the digital version. The game needs up to 212 GB of free space. It unlocks at 12 a.m. local time on Thursday, Nov. 19, so some US players can start at midnight on Wednesday, Nov. 18, depending on time zone. Pre-loading does not let you play early.

Why has the launch drawn criticism?

The game was delayed twice, from fall 2025 to May 2026 and then to November. Gameplay footage leaked in August. The digital-only release has also frustrated players who say downloads do not equal permanent ownership. A PC version is expected later.

What does it mean for Take-Two?

Shares closed at $231.31 on Nov. 11, up 8.3% since earnings but down about 10% this year. The average analyst target is $290. Take-Two kept its fiscal 2027 bookings outlook at $8 billion to $8.2 billion. First official sales figures usually arrive within days of launch.

What is not confirmed?

The preorder figures are estimates. Sources differ on when physical edition download codes go on sale, listed as Nov. 12 in one report, and on how a digital-only release applies to those editions. This is not investment advice.
